observations: A standing rule is only ever the producer's own stated decision: an inferred one is refused with its reason, and so is keeping the same decision twice.

In a later project the rule arrives as a `stated` decision whose sourceRef is producer_memory:<id>, so it outranks research and inference but is visible and can be overridden by anything said in that project.
Revoking stops later projects inheriting it and leaves the briefs it already shaped exactly as they were; the revoked row stays listed for the record.
Explanations are assembled from the stored plan, the brief and the last edit; no model is called on this path.

The endpoint explains the project's LATEST plan. The dev project's latest arrangement (v8) came from a full generation, not from PR-U5's edit, so no plan.regeneration evidence appears in this run; the regeneration lines are covered by the unit suite. A version-scoped explanation is not implemented.
